standard_prerequisites.name: Support of a finite type module on a fibre
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-support-finite-type (canonical Stacks tag 056J); invoked at proof line 474
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that Supp(F_s) = V(I(B tensor_A kappa(p))); the choice of f_1, ..., f_m cutting out that closed set is inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Translate to algebra and identify the support: with f given by A -> B and F by the finite B-module M whose annihilator is I, use the annihilator description of the support and the fibre description of F_s to write Supp(F_s) = V(I(B tensor_A kappa(p))) (proof lines 458-476).

Make the closed set finitely presented: since B tensor_A kappa(p) is of finite type over kappa(p) and the support there is cut out by the ideal generated by I, choose finitely many f_1, ..., f_m in I whose images generate that ideal (proof lines 476-483).

Build the closed immersion and its module: let Z = Spec(B/(f_1, ..., f_m)) with i : Z -> X the closed immersion cut out by (f_1, ..., f_m); since M is annihilated by I it is a B/(f_1, ..., f_m)-module, so F is the pushforward of a finite type module G on Z, while Z_s = Supp(F_s) holds by construction and i is of finite presentation (proof lines 484-490).
proof_roadmap: Affine algebra setup: write f as A -> B and F as M~ for the finite B-module M with annihilator I, so that Supp(F) = V(I) (proof lines 458-468).
Fibre computation: with q the prime of B over x and p the prime of A over s, the fibre F_s corresponds to M tensor_A kappa(p), whose support is V(I(B tensor_A kappa(p))) (proof lines 469-476).

Finite presentation of the support: finite generation of B tensor_A kappa(p) over kappa(p) gives f_1, ..., f_m in I generating that ideal, and Z = Spec(B/(f_1, ..., f_m)) with its closed immersion i satisfies Z_s = Supp(F_s) and i_*G = F for G = M~ viewed as a module on Z (proof lines 476-490).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the algebraised existence statement behind the chapter's key technical lemma: given a finite type morphism of affine schemes with a finite type module F, it produces a finitely presented closed immersion i : Z -> X together with a finite type module G on Z whose pushforward is F and whose fibre Z_s is exactly Supp(F_s) (statement lines 451-454). The substance is the conversion of the fibre support, which is a priori only a closed subset of the fibre, into a finitely generated ideal inside the annihilator of M: finite generation of B tensor_A kappa(p) over kappa(p) is what supplies finitely many f_1, ..., f_m whose span already computes the support on the fibre, and only then can Z be defined by a finitely presented closed immersion (proof lines 476-488). The remaining steps are direct translations between modules and their associated sheaves, so the claim is H2. Note that the pinned author text writes the generating tuple once as (f_1, ..., f_m) and once as (f_1, ..., f_n); this is reproduced verbatim and not corrected.
